our_argument_summary: WIN-069 claims V13 two-zone topology + aetheric refraction validates Australian road distances (6.2% cross-equatorial RMSE, 10.2% same-hemisphere mean error; AGD66→GDA94 as topology evidence). Our review (verdict Misleading) argues: (1) road excess over geodesic is a terrain-and-circuity property, not topology; (2) 6.2% RMSE expressed in absolute positional terms is ~5 orders of magnitude worse than routine sub-m geodesy on a 4,000 km baseline, with the finding now adding a (mis-rounded — see hole H0) relative-error parallel; (3) AGD66→GDA94 is standard regional→geocentric datum evolution, not topology evidence; (4) V13 parameters (a = π×R_Earth, H(r) fits) are calibrated against globe data, so the 'validation' is circular; (5) terrain-based road-network analysis (Giacomin & Levinson 2015 descriptive circuity; OSRM tooling Huber & Rust 2016) outperforms V13 on in-sample road-distance recovery. The c8 state confirms c7's three patchable holes (H1/H2/H3) are now landed in the data, but the H3 closure introduced one new internal-rounding asymmetry that this cycle catches as a c8 minor hole.

holes_found.description: Lens C arithmetic asymmetry inside the finding. The clause now reads: '6.2% RMSE is ~5 orders of magnitude worse than sub-meter geodesy in absolute positional terms (and ~6 orders of magnitude worse in relative distance error on a 4,000 km baseline)'. Both halves of this sentence are derived from the SAME arithmetic ratio. Absolute: V13 positional error 6.2% × 4,000 km = 248 km = 2.48×10^5 m; sub-meter geodesy ≤ 1 m absolute; ratio 2.48×10^5; log10 = 5.394 → '~5 orders' (✓). Relative: V13 fractional 6.2×10^-2; sub-meter on 4,000 km baseline = 1 m / 4×10^6 m = 2.5×10^-7 fractional; ratio 6.2×10^-2 / 2.5×10^-7 = 2.48×10^5; log10 = 5.394 → should also be '~5 orders', NOT '~6 orders'. The two ratios are mathematically identical when 'sub-meter' is taken consistently as ≤ 1 m absolute. The '~6 orders' framing in the parenthetical can only be justified if 'sub-meter' is silently re-interpreted as ~0.1 m (decimeter-class) for the relative half while remaining ~1 m for the absolute half — but that asymmetric interpretation is not stated and would require the absolute half to also be '~6 orders'. The result is that a careful dome defender (or an AI parsing the page narratively) can score a free 'your own arithmetic is internally inconsistent — log10(2.48×10^5)=5.39, not 6' rebuttal. This is also inconsistent with detail_evidence ¶2, which uses 'roughly five orders of magnitude larger than standard sub-meter geodetic positioning (~250,000×)' — the same ~5.39 ratio rounded to 5. The chain that produced this rounding error: c7 stronger_arguments[0] said 'roughly 6 orders of magnitude smaller than 6.2%' (already off by ~0.6 orders); c7 H3 preemptive_recommendation cited the same number; ISS-2777 disposition repeated it; EXP-630 patch description repeated 'giving ~6 orders of magnitude gap'; analyst-baby integrated verbatim. This is a curmudgeon-introduced rounding error that has now propagated into published text via the c7→ISS-2777→EXP-630→ca0fd35 chain.
holes_found.recommendation: Lowest-cost fix: change '~6 orders of magnitude worse in relative distance error' to '~5 orders of magnitude worse in relative distance error' so both halves of the finding round the identical log10=5.39 ratio identically and align with detail_evidence ¶2's 'roughly five orders' framing. Alternative (preserves the parallel-construction intent without the rounding mismatch): replace the parenthetical with 'i.e., a fractional distance error of ~6×10^-2 versus ≤2.5×10^-7 for sub-meter geodesy on the same baseline' — gives the reader the actual ratio inputs and lets them count orders themselves. If the dome's '~6 orders' claim is intended to compare against decimeter-class differential GNSS (~0.1 m) rather than meter-class sub-meter (~1 m), say so explicitly: 'or ~6 orders worse if the comparison is to decimeter-class differential GNSS' — but at that point you may as well step the comparison through the sub-m→cm→mm→sub-mm ladder (the c7 stronger_arguments already drafted this with ~8 orders for mm-GNSS and ~9 orders for sub-mm VLBI). The argument's headline does NOT depend on this distinction — V13 loses to standard geodesy by 5+ orders under every interpretation, so the fix is purely cosmetic-arithmetic hygiene. Low priority but worth catching before the asymmetry calcifies in subsequent reviews.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model correctly identifies that road distances systematically exceed great-circle (geodesic) distances across transcontinental Australia, and correctly identifies that AGD66 was non-geocentric by design — both are real geographic facts (data/wins.json:069 detail_evidence ¶1 cites Norseman–Ceduna ≈1.07 and the 90-Mile Straight's <0.005% deviation, and ¶3 cites usq.pressbooks.pub/gpsandgnss/chapter/2-2-australian-datums/ for AGD66's non-geocentric design). The V13 two-zone topology is a creative attempt to model the road excess by allowing the equatorial ring radius to absorb the residual.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Both facts admit standard explanations without dome topology. Road excess is a terrain and network-circuity property documented across every continent (data/wins.json:069 detail_evidence ¶5 cites Giacomin & Levinson 2015 DOI 10.1068/b130131p for mean circuities ~1.19 across 51 US MSAs). AGD66→GDA94 is a routine regional→geocentric datum transition every continent performed (data/wins.json:069 detail_evidence ¶3 cites en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geocentric_Datum_of_Australia_1994). The V13 prediction is calibrated against globe distances (a = π×R_Earth ≈ 20,015 km — Lens C this run verifies π×6,371 = 20,015.087 km to 5 sig figs against the dome's stated value). None of the three observations — road excess, 6.2% RMSE, datum shift — discriminates between dome topology and standard terrain-plus-geocentric-geodesy.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender accepting our methodological principles (internal consistency first, discriminatory power required, no default favoritism) would attack on the c8-flagged arithmetic-internal-consistency surface: 'Your finding now claims, in a single sentence, that the 6.2% RMSE is ~5 orders of magnitude worse than sub-meter geodesy in absolute positional terms AND ~6 orders worse in relative distance error on the same 4,000 km baseline. Those two numbers come from the same ratio — 6.2% divided by (1 m / 4,000 km) = 248,000, log10 = 5.394. You round 5.394 down to 5 in one half of the sentence and round it up to 6 in the other half. Your detail_evidence ¶2 says ''roughly five orders of magnitude larger... (~250,000×)'' — explicitly 5. By your own first methodological principle, internal consistency, you have an internal inconsistency in the finding the page leads with. If your headline orders-of-magnitude claim varies depending on which half of the same sentence the reader looks at, why should we trust the magnitude framing at all? More substantively: the comparison you actually want is V13 in-sample 10.2% vs. terrain-based circuity 5-15% in-sample. That parity comparison is in detail_evidence ¶5 but isn''t in the finding or TLDRs. You have the right argument; you''ve buried it.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Fix the arithmetic asymmetry per H0 recommendation (change '~6 orders' to '~5 orders' in the finding's relative-error parallel, OR replace the parenthetical with the explicit fractional ratio '6×10^-2 vs ≤2.5×10^-7 on the same baseline'). The defender's stronger second pivot — that the in-sample parity comparison (V13 10.2% vs. circuity 5-15%) is buried in detail_evidence ¶5 — was already noted in c7's deeper_analysis but never patched. A separate parallel hole (not flagged here as severity gate is hole H0's arithmetic) is that the surfaced finding still leads with the orders-of-magnitude framing rather than the like-for-like in-sample parity. Defense_survives=3 because the arithmetic-inconsistency rebuttal is structurally coherent, concedes nothing on the dome's side, and exploits a real inconsistency on our side; but the underlying argument (V13 is hopelessly worse than standard geodesy under every plausible rounding) survives intact. Severity 3 not 4 because the fix is one word ('5' for '6') and the defense doesn't change the verdict.

quantitative_verification.computations: All computed independently this run via python3. (1) π × 6,371 km = 20,015.087 km — matches the dome's stated disc radius a = 20,015 km to 5 sig figs. (2) 6.2% × 4,000 km = 248 km = 2.48×10^5 m — confirms the 'hundreds of km positional error on transcontinental routes' framing. (3) Absolute ratio: 2.48×10^5 m / 1 m = 2.48×10^5 → log10 = 5.394 → '~5 orders' ✓. (4) Relative ratio: 6.2×10^-2 / (1 m / 4×10^6 m) = 6.2×10^-2 / 2.5×10^-7 = 2.48×10^5 → log10 = 5.394 → SHOULD also be '~5 orders'. The finding's '~6 orders' is mis-rounded (see hole H0). (5) The IDENTITY abs_ratio = rel_ratio holds exactly when the 'sub-meter' baseline is held consistent — the ratios are the same number. Alternative interpretation: if sub-meter is taken as 0.1 m (decimeter-class), both halves give log10 = 6.394 → '~6 orders' for BOTH; the asymmetric framing is defensible under no consistent interpretation. (6) Arc-vs-chord deviation for a 146.6 km segment on R=6378 km: L²/(24R²) ≈ 9.4×10^-6 ≈ 0.0009% (the order is ~10^-5, looser to ~10^-3 if you use small-angle approximations) — the dome's road IS the chord, so 'deviates from its great-circle geodesic by less than 0.005%' is now in the conservative tight-bound regime per c7 H2 / ISS-1500 / ISS-2776 / ISS-2778 — verified resolved in all three places (detail_evidence, tldr_evidence, tldr_verdict). All other numerical claims in the WIN are verified accurate.

Under no single consistent interpretation of 'sub-meter' does the asymmetric '5 absolute, 6 relative' framing hold. Flagged as hole H0 above. The 0.005% geodesic-deviation tightening is verified in all three places (resolves c7 H2 / c6 H3 / ISS-1500 / ISS-2776 / ISS-2778).

deeper_analysis:
This c8 cycle is the post-patch baseline of the c7 H1/H2/H3 closures. Three c7 holes were closed by interleaved patches in the c7→c8 window: ISS-2775 (c7 H1, fc962ec 2026-06-15T02:26Z, 'thousands of possible' → 'larger set of major transcontinental'), ISS-2776+ISS-2778 (c7 H2, fc962ec + 70225ce 2026-06-15→16, '0.4%' → '0.005%' propagated across detail_evidence, tldr_evidence, tldr_verdict), and ISS-2777 (c7 H3, EXP-630 → ca0fd35 2026-06-15T15:37Z, relative-error parallel added to finding). The c7 H0 / c6 H1 / ISS-1498 thread is soft-resolved by the 'in-sample' qualifier addition that occurred earlier; current text reads 'single-digit-percent in-sample residuals' which materially weakens the original c7 H0 concern; the residual 'no inline citation' sub-concern persists at minor severity but was already marked no-action in c7. Mechanically, all four c7 holes are addressed in the current text.

The one c8 finding is a Lens C arithmetic-internal-consistency issue introduced by the ISS-2777 patch itself. The patch description in EXP-630-baby-batch-2.json says 'The relative-error comparison: sub-meter on 4000 km baseline ≈ 2.5e-7 vs 6.2% ≈ 6e-2, giving ~6 orders of magnitude gap.' That arithmetic is wrong: log10(6e-2 / 2.5e-7) = log10(2.4×10^5) = 5.38, not 6. The error originated in c7 stronger_arguments[0] ('roughly 6 orders of magnitude smaller than 6.2%'), propagated through c7 H3 preemptive_recommendation, ISS-2777 disposition, and into the integrated patch verbatim. As a result, the finding now claims the same identical ratio is '~5 orders' in its first half and '~6 orders' in its second half — a within-sentence internal inconsistency that contradicts detail_evidence ¶2's 'roughly five orders of magnitude larger... (~250,000×)' framing. Severity is minor because the headline argument (V13 loses to geodesy by 5+ orders under every interpretation) is unchanged, and the fix is one word ('5' for '6') or a short reframe; but it is worth catching before further reviews calcify the asymmetry. Lens A (advocate mode) confirms a dome defender would score a free rebuttal off this inconsistency (defense_survives=3); fix per H0 closes it.

Lens B (cross-WIN consistency) verifies that the WIN-027/057/069 cluster is internally consistent at verdict level (all three Misleading) and the EXP-630 patch made the WIN-057↔WIN-069 cross-WIN labeling MORE symmetric (each WIN now carries the appropriate error-frame label for its argument shape). The c8 H0 issue is intra-WIN, not cross-WIN.

Lens C all-greens the WIN's other numerical claims: π × 6,371 = 20,015.087 km matches dome's a = 20,015 km to 5 sig figs; 6.2% × 4,000 km = 248 km positional error; 248,000 m / 1 m = 2.48×10^5 supports the '~250,000×' multiplier; and the new 0.005% geodesic-deviation tightening verifies as conservatively bounding the true ~10^-5 chord-arc deviation. The H2 closure is mechanically correct in all three text places.

Verdict 'Misleading' continues to hold. The TLDR fields and detail_verdict_text accurately summarize the post-patch detail content. The H0 minor asymmetry does not affect verdict, kill-shot status, or the broader page argument — only the precision of one within-sentence rounding inside the WIN-069 finding.
